title: Creating and scaling your own custom copilots with Azure AI Studio: Hanchi Wang
talk_summary: A Microsoft engineer demos Azure AI Studio + Prompt Flow for building a SQL/chart chatbot, emphasizing three capabilities: OpenTelemetry-based tracing with a local trace-viewer UI, dataset-driven evaluation (built-in content-safety evaluators plus custom Python evaluators like execution time, error rate, SQL similarity), and production monitoring dashboards. The core transferable idea is wrapping agent/tool calls in trace decorators and running the same eval dataset across candidate models to pick by measured accuracy/cost/latency rather than vibes.

takeaways.technique: Same-dataset model comparison to drive routing decisions
takeaways.what_they_do: Run one fixed eval dataset (question + ground-truth SQL) through multiple candidate models and compare execution time, error rate, and similarity-to-ground-truth side by side, then pick the model based on whether speed or accuracy matters.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I have a custom data set and I want to evaluate the same data set across different models
takeaways.numbers: Compared GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4-turbo, Mistral-large on execution time, error rate, SQL similarity

takeaways.technique: Custom evaluators as code, not just LLM-judge scores
takeaways.what_they_do: Beyond built-in safety evaluators, they write plain Python evaluator functions (execution time, error rate, similarity to ground truth) and plug them into an evaluate() harness that links dataset + target + evaluators.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the three evaluators following are customer evaluators which give me execution time error rate and S SEO similarity scores

takeaways.technique: Trace decorator on every tool/LLM call, OpenTelemetry-native
takeaways.what_they_do: A single @trace decorator on any Python function emits OpenTelemetry spans capturing inputs/outputs and auto-captures LLM interactions; a local UI shows the full nested trace (outer app -> tool -> generated SQL -> code interpreter) for debugging.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the trace decorator helps um to emate uh events uh emit traces to capture inputs outputs and events of Pyon function

takeaways.technique: Token-usage dashboard split prompt vs completion
takeaways.what_they_do: Production dashboard shows model duration and token usage broken into prompt vs completion tokens, revealing where cost concentrates.
takeaways.evidence_quote: majority of the tokens are actually used for the prompt uh and only a few are for the completion so if we are concerned about the cost then maybe we need to uh short The Prompt templates

takeaways.technique: Local trace-viewer test harness before deploy
takeaways.what_they_do: A CLI command points at the entry function and launches a local UI to run a question and watch traces stream in live, so engineers debug the agent loop locally before touching cloud.
takeaways.evidence_quote: prf flow provides a local UI just for that

takeaways.technique: Synthetic test-data generation for eval sets
takeaways.what_they_do: Prompt Flow includes tooling to generate synthetic test datasets when hand-written eval data is missing, pairing question and ground-truth columns.
takeaways.evidence_quote: proml has a suite of tools to help you to generate a synthetic test data set
